experiments.name: Conditioning ablation (types / plain / dropout)
experiments.blurb: ry type conditioning shows NO benefit; the only significant effect is prompt-format mismatch. Dropout wins by robustness (never mismatched).
experiments.verdict: Paired t: types conditioning -0.005 (t=-0.87, n.s.); mismatch -0.018 (t=-3.12, sig).

experiments.name: Drafting families (v3) — comment & roxygen
experiments.blurb: The clearest positive result: the drafting families teach drafting; the control can't even produce the right kind of output.
experiments.verdict: Control writes code instead of comments. Judge calibrated (GT 100% score-2, unrelated 100% score-0).

experiments.name: Scenario-family eval (v3 vs control)
experiments.blurb: Every programmatic family is learned and transfers to held-out packages (3%-per-family package holdout, exact validators).

experiments.name: v4 — finish-block upweight (allocation experiment)
experiments.blurb: Capability tracks training share in BOTH directions: +15% whole-region, roxygen drafting halved. Midtyping flat (4th datapoint). Conclusion: train longer, don't reweight.

experiments.name: SFT v5 — suffix convention + no_op + mid_roxygen + cursor fix
experiments.blurb: ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET. The live-session regression cases (sd-line echo, post-brace eagerness, mom-glue, mid-roxygen) flipped from 0 to pass. Best model on every capability metric.
experiments.verdict: Data bugs fixed en route: scenario rows had silently lost their cursor marker since v2 (char-vs-line index); edit_pairs re-emitted region heads.

experiments.name: Intent-assertion suite (Zed-style)
experiments.blurb: 44 plain-English behavioral tests, glm-5.3 judge, calibration-gated. The user's live bugs became permanent regression tests.

experiments.name: Matryoshka gate probe
experiments.blurb: Layer-prefix extraction works (12-layer prefix of Qwen3.5-2B converted to GGUF), but our llama.cpp build's converter hard-requires the MTP head. FIXED in llama.cpp main (--no-nextn/--mtp flags) — rebuild queued.
experiments.verdict: Strategy alive: Matryoshka validated at 0.5/1.5/3B with -36% compute and +14-26% spec-decode throughput (arXiv 2608.09703).

experiments.name: Architecture dossier v1
experiments.blurb: Recommendation (prior to beat): dense GDN 3:1 hybrid, 32K R-vocab, 1 MTP layer, Matryoshka tiers 0.7/1.3/2.6B @ d=2560. Vocab math: lm_head reads 82MB vs 635MB per token (32K vs 248K). Hermes red-team running with the convenience-is-not-an-argument mandate.
experiments.verdict: Standing rule recorded: effort is never a blocker; convenience must not pick the architecture.

decisions: Suffix-completion convention everywhere: predict ONLY what comes after the cursor (user decision; finish-block re-emission retired).
Dropout conditioning is the production config — justified by robustness to prompt population, not type signal (ablation showed none).
Telemetry: local collection always, upload never — until an explicit opt-in (off by default).
Eval battery: acceptance counters (extension) > validator-exact scenario families + calibrated judge + intent assertions > line-F1 midtyping (composition-blind, 4 datapoints).
Effort is never a blocker; llama.cpp support is deployment evidence, not selection criteria. Wide architecture space gets a genuine pass.
Quota discipline: max 6-8 concurrent zai consumers; Gemini (agy) and Opus 4.6 (separate quota) for free-tier generation; Opus reserved for high-judgment tasks.
Ops: llama-server evals CPU-only; readiness via POST /v1/completions (never /health); kill by tracked PID/port only; GPU jobs strictly sequential (flock, not memory polls — the 03:20 incident).
